newsitem.title: DENMARK: Carlsberg says to buy Bass' Carlsberg-Tetley stake.
newsitem.headline: Carlsberg says to buy Bass' Carlsberg-Tetley stake.

text.p: Danish brewer Carlsberg said Friday it would buy the 50 percent stake held by its British partner Bass in their Carlsberg-Tetley alliance for 110 million pounds ($183 million).
The announcment followed a British government ruling that blocked Bass's planned purchase of Carslberg's half of the joint venture.
"Obviously, we are disappointed with the decision announced by the UK President of the Board of Trade," Carlsberg International Managing Director Michael Iuul said in a statement.

But, he added, Carlsberg had known that stiff monitoring of the British brewing industry by competition authorities meant the deal might be blocked. He added that Carlsberg had found areas of savings within Carlsberg-Tetley that could be implemented without Bass.
"The fundamental structural reorganization to be implemented in Carlsberg-Tetley within the next few years will obviously involve expenses for the company," he said.

"However, it should be taken into consideration that Carlsberg will be taking over a 50 percent interest in the company for 110 million pounds ($183 million), which is substantially below the market value."

Carlsberg-Tetley Managing Director Ebbe Dinesen said the company was disappointed at the British decision but at the same time relieved that seven months of uncertainty while British monopoly watchdogs deliberated was over.
"Now we can get down to work and get on with business," he said in an interview.
The original deal would have made Bass Britain's biggest brewer, giving it 35 percent of the domestic beer market.

Margaret Beckett, the Labour government's new Trade and Industry Secretary, said in a statement issued Friday that she disagreed with the Monopolies and Mergers Commission view that the negative effects of the merger could be dealt with by demanding the sale of 1,900 Bass pubs.
Bass' existing market share of the British market is 23 percent, below Scottish and Newcastle Plc, which makes 29 of every 100 pints consumed.
Under the original terms of the deal, announced last August, Bass paid 200 million pounds ($333 million) for the 50 percent interest in Carlsberg-Tetley owned by drinks group Allied Domecq.
Carlsberg agreed to contribute its interest to Bass, together with 20 million pounds ($33 million), in exchange for 20 percent of the merged Bass Brewers/Carlsberg-Tetley business.
